title: Normalize and validate properties with the C# field keyword
goal: Use C# 14's field keyword to normalize or validate values in a property setter without declaring a separate backing field. Apply when property assignments need trimming, case conversion or input checks, while preserving constructor validation and the behavior of an explicit-field implementation.

routes.sdk: 10.0.402 (verification baseline; .NET 10 SDK with C# 14 support required)
prerequisites: Target net10.0 with a supported .NET 10 SDK; no preview language mode or workloads required.
constraints: The field keyword is C# 14 syntax; use the explicit-field comparison for .NET 9 / C# 13.
Assigning the property inside its own setter recursively invokes that setter. Write field instead.
A property initializer writes the backing field directly and does not execute the setter. Assign through the property in the constructor when initial input must be validated.
This example has no synchronization; concurrent mutation needs a separate design.

prerequisites: Install the stated .NET 11 SDK separately, keep TargetFramework=net10.0 and LangVersion=14.0, and provide the .NET 10 targeting pack/runtime. This route is optional; the .NET 10 SDK route remains valid. No C# 15-on-.NET 10 compatibility is claimed.
